title: Cap. IV Arg. 6 Sol: elect known a posteriori — many elect while still unbelieving; Rom. 8:28–30
pass_a_gloss: Solution. When the sacred Scriptures speak of certain designated persons as of the Elect, they accommodate this word to believers alone: because we have nothing certain concerning the secret of Election except from the posterior, that is, from the effects of faith and sanctification. Hence the Apostle is accustomed everywhere to mark believers with the name of the Elect. But thence it is not brought about either that the elect and believers ought to be confused, or that election ought to be suspended from foresight of faith as an antecedent condition. For although we cannot call those elect whom we see unbelieving, yet it is certain that many impenitent and unbelieving are nonetheless meanwhile elect: which in Paul, and so in all the elect, before efficacious conversion, is most true. Moreover since the words of Predestination and Election are used promiscuously in this whole disputation, it is plain that the word of the Predestinated, when it is treated concerning salvation, is used even of unbelievers. For when the Apostle at Rom. 8:28 says, Whom he Predestinated, he Called; whom he called he justified, etc., he openly places certain Predestinated antecedently to vocation, faith, and justification.
pass_b_english: Sol. When Scripture names designated persons Elect, it fits the word to believers alone — because we know nothing sure of election's secret except a posteriori, from the effects of faith and sanctification. So the Apostle often marks believers as Elect. That does not mean elect and believers must be confused, or that election hangs on foresight of faith as an antecedent condition. We cannot call unbelievers elect as we see them — yet many impenitent and unbelieving are elect in the meantime; true of Paul and of all the elect before efficacious conversion. And since Predestination and Election are used interchangeably in this dispute, Predestinated in salvation-talk is used even of unbelievers. Rom. 8:28ff.: Whom he predestinated, he called; whom he called, he justified — openly sets some Predestinated before vocation, faith, and justification.
source_text: Sol. Quando sacrae Scripturae loquuntur de aliquibus designatis personis tanquam de Electis, hoc vocabulum accommodant ad solos credentes: quia nos de arcano Electionis nihil certi habemus nisi a posteriore, hoc est, ab effectis fidei et sanctificationis. Hinc Apostolus credentes Electorum nomine passim solet notare. Verum inde non efficitur, vel debere confundi electos et credentes, vel electionem ex praevisa fide tanquam conditione antecedanea esse suspendendam. Quamvis enim nos non possumus eos electos vocare, quos videmus incredulos, tamen certum est, multos impoenitentes ac incredulos esse tamen interim electos: quod in Paulo, adeoque in omnibus electis, ante efficacem conversionem, verissimum est. Quin etiam cum Praedestinationis et Electionis vocabula in tota hac disputatione promiscue usurpentur, planum est vocem Praedestinatorum, cum de salute agitur, etiam de incredulis usurpari. Nam cum Apostolus Rom. viii. 28. dicit, Quos Praedestinavit, Vocavit; quos vocavit justificavit, &c. aperte ponit Praedestinatos quosdam antecedenter ad vocationem, fidem et justificationem.
